prompt_en: Create a photorealistic cinematic photograph in a vast closed clock museum during a lunar eclipse. An unmistakably adult woman works as the living clock conservator. Her visible facial proportions, long dark wavy hair, and natural styling follow the reference portrait. Preserve the reference portrait as the sole identity source, keeping her facial geometry, eye aperture, eye shape and spacing, eyebrows, nose, lips, face length, lower-face and jaw width, cheekbones, skin tone, natural asymmetry, hairline, and adult age unchanged. Across from her stands an embodied skeletal personification of Death in a weathered ceremonial mantle; an embodied skeletal personification of Death acts as an agent. Death deliberately turns the final hourglass and the last illuminated numeral on a terminal clock goes dark beneath its bony hand. Death deliberately turns the final hourglass with both bony hands; the affected terminal clock visibly goes dark. A wilted cut flower releases one final petal beside the clock; vanitas objects support rather than replace the active agent. Compose the woman, active Death figure, hourglass, extinguished numeral, and falling petal in one readable wide frame with cold eclipse light and warm dying clock lamps. Use a low oblique 35 mm viewpoint and triangular depth between witness, agent, and clock; an eclipse rim separates Death's bones while the dying amber numeral remains the sole warm focal pool.
negative_en: excessive HDR, over-processed retouching, illustration look, 3D render look, low resolution, fake-looking background, warped product geometry, cartoon style, inaccurate reflections
